The (In,Ga)As cores were grown at 500°C, while the (Ga,Mn)As shells were deposited at 220°C.
The (In,Ga)As cores contain around 10% In, while the (Ga,Mn)As shells contain 5% Mn.
The nanowires are vertically oriented with respect to the GaAs(111)B substrate, up to 1.6 μm long, and have diameters of 70-100 nm.
The nanowire density is high, around 2 x 10^9 NWs/cm^2.
TEM analysis shows a sharp, coherent interface between the (In,Ga)As core and (Ga,Mn)As shell, with no misfit dislocations.
Some nanowires contain a low density of basal stacking faults, mainly at the ends.
The (Ga,Mn)As shells exhibit ferromagnetic coupling at temperatures above 33 K, but the overall behavior is superparamagnetic.
The (Ga,Mn)As shell growth rate is much lower (20 nm/h) than the planar growth rate (200 nm/h).
A (Ga,Mn)As layer up to 70 nm thick was also deposited between the nanowires.
Raman spectroscopy estimates the In content in the (In,Ga)As cores to be around 12 ± 4%.
The absence of GaAs-like LO phonon mode in the Raman spectra indicates the high quality of the (In,Ga)As cores.
The wurtzite crystal structure of the nanowires is different from the typical zinc-blende structure in planar thin films.
Ferromagnetic nanowires are of interest for memory device applications, particularly for controlling magnetic domain walls.
Magnetic measurements on the nanowire samples required careful separation from the substrate and other magnetic contributions.
The two-stage MBE growth approach allows incorporation of high Mn content in the (Ga,Mn)As shells.
